title: Scoped entitlement lifecycle and federated provisioning classification (SSO / SCIM / RBAC)
creator: Lena Park
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers submit a wide range of admin/access requests (role grants, SCIM sync fixes, SSO mapping changes, org-level policy exceptions). Current intake is ad hoc: emails, tickets in multiple systems, and inconsistent routing. This leads to long lead times, audit gaps, and costly manual triage.

Goal: Define a deterministic classification and routing system for admin/access requests that covers scoped entitlements (role templates, resource scopes), federated provisioning (SSO attribute mappings, SCIM user/group flows), and org-policy exceptions. Deliver a low-risk auto-provision path, clear manual-review gates for high-risk requests, and telemetry for SLA and auditability.

Proposed deliverables:
- Classification matrix (risk buckets: low / medium / high) mapping request types to default RBAC templates, required evidence, and owner teams.
- Standardized intake form (Confluence + intake UI) with machine-readable fields to populate scoring rules.
- Scoring rules engine (heuristics first: resource sensitivity, role privileges, requester affiliation) to auto-route or flag for manual review.
- Auto-provision workflow for low-risk requests with configurable time-windowed rollback and audit logging.
- Manual review runbook for medium/high requests with checklist items for security, legal, and account teams.
- Observability dashboard (SLOs: mean time to decision, approval rates, reverts) and per-tenant audit trails exported to customer KMS/Audit.

Success metrics (90-day):
- 50% of incoming admin requests auto-provisioned within SLA (TTR < 4 hours).
- Mean manual triage time reduced by 40%.
- 100% of approvals recorded with required evidence for audit.
- Zero customer-facing mis-provision incidents in first 90 days after rollout.

Trade-offs and constraints:
- Automation reduces latency but increases blast-radius risk; mitigations include conservative scoring thresholds, one-hour soft-rollbacks, and easy remediation path.
- SCIM / SSO vendor differences force a subset of config that maps to our canonical model; non-conforming customers require a manual adapter path.
- RBAC templating must balance expressiveness with simplicity to avoid role explosion.

Rollout plan:
1) Build classification matrix and intake form (internal pilot with 3 existing enterprise customers).
2) Implement scoring rules + telemetry (feature-flagged for pilot tenants).
3) Ship auto-provision for low-risk requests + runbook for manual review.
4) Expand to broader cohort and tune thresholds, add SCIM mapping templates.

Stakeholders: Security, SRE, Identity Integrations (Eng), Solution Engineering, Customer Success, Legal.

Acceptance criteria:
- Classification matrix published in Confluence and onboarded with 3 pilot accounts.
- Intake form captures formalized fields and populates the scoring engine payload.
- Dashboard shows request volume, auto-approve rate, mean decision time, and revert counts.
- Security sign-off obtained and documented on the runbook.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Confluence doc with classification matrix and examples. 2) Intake form + JSON payload schema committed. 3) Scoring engine prototype accepting real pilot traffic. 4) Observability dashboard with baseline metrics. 5) Security and legal sign-off for auto-provision rules.
